title: The beauty and simplicity of Normal

cues.en: Instructor: There is a real beauty and a kind of bizarreness to mathematics and statistics.
cues.zh: 數學與統計有真正的美，也有某種奇妙之處。

cues.en: And people often get sidetracked with math because they're thinking about the very practical hands-on applications of math.
cues.zh: 人們常被數學很實際、可操作的用途分散注意力。

cues.en: And how can I use applied math like statistics to help me be a better data scientist, to help me get a better job, to help me understand what I'm doing with my data sets and so on.
cues.zh: 例如如何用統計這類應用數學，成為更好的資料科學家、找到更好的工作、理解資料集的處理等。

cues.en: But I want to take a few moments of your time to go on a little bit of a tangent just to talk about how incredibly beautiful
cues.zh: 但想花你一點時間，稍微離題，談談常態，

cues.en: the normal AKA standard AKA Gaussian distribution really is.
cues.zh: 也稱標準、高斯分布，究竟有多麼美。

cues.en: So we start off with a function, a formula that looks like this.
cues.zh: 從這個函數、公式開始。

cues.en: This is the complete version of the Gaussian formula, including the normalization factor, including various parameters that you can include that will change the shape and the scale
cues.zh: 這是完整高斯公式，包含正規化因子，以及能改變高斯函數形狀、尺度，

cues.en: and the location of the Gaussian function.
cues.zh: 與位置的各種參數。

cues.en: But you know, a lot of this stuff is unnecessary.
cues.zh: 但很多其實不必要。

cues.en: A lot of this stuff is just added complexity.
cues.zh: 很多只是額外的複雜性。

cues.en: You can actually boil down this function to its core skeleton, to the most meaningful and essential parts, and that actually just looks like this
cues.zh: 可以化約到核心骨架，最有意義、最根本的部分，看起來就是，

cues.en: e to the minus x squared.
cues.zh: e的−x²次方。

cues.en: Now, this we can make a plot of, we can put the value of this function on the y axis and this value x, or it's sometimes also t on the x axis.
cues.zh: 可以畫圖，把函數值放y軸，x，有時也寫t，放x軸。

cues.en: And that looks like this.
cues.zh: 看起來像這樣。

cues.en: This gives us the normal distribution.
cues.zh: 得到常態分布。

cues.en: It's also called the standard distribution.
cues.zh: 也叫標準分布。

cues.en: It's sometimes called the bell curve, and it's also called the Gaussian because it was Carl Gauss, the brilliant mathematician who developed this and sort of derived this equation
cues.zh: 有時叫鐘形曲線，也叫高斯，因為才華洋溢的數學家Carl Gauss發展、推導了這個公式，

cues.en: and a lot of properties about it.
cues.zh: 以及許多性質。

cues.en: Now, the graph itself is beautiful in its simplicity.
cues.zh: 圖本身的簡單，就很美。

cues.en: It is smooth everywhere.
cues.zh: 處處平滑。

cues.en: It's continuous everywhere and is perfectly symmetric around its peak.
cues.zh: 處處連續，而且以峰為中心，完全對稱。

cues.en: And there's nothing sort of threatening or frightening.
cues.zh: 沒有威脅或可怕之處。

cues.en: It's a very friendly, gentle curve.
cues.zh: 是非常友善、溫和的曲線。

cues.en: And then if we look at this basic formula here, the essence of the Gaussian formula, it's also just visually beautiful.
cues.zh: 再看這個基本公式，高斯公式的精髓，視覺上也很美。

cues.en: It's aesthetically pleasing to look at.
cues.zh: 看起來很賞心悅目。

cues.en: We have three terms here, e, x, and 2 and they all go up in a line like this.
cues.zh: 有三項，e、x與2，像這樣排成向上的線。

cues.en: And each term is in the exponent of the previous term.
cues.zh: 每一項都在前一項的指數上。

cues.en: So we have e to the power of x and then x to the power of 2.
cues.zh: 先是e的x次方，再是x的2次方。

cues.en: There's just a, a beauty in the way that this equation looks.
cues.zh: 公式的樣貌，本身就有種美。

cues.en: The remarkable thing is that this little formula here, this Gaussian equation, is the basis of most statistics.
cues.zh: 驚人的是，這個小小的高斯公式，是大部分統計的基礎。

cues.en: Not all statistics, of course, it's richer than this, but almost everything in statistics can be somehow related back to this really simple expression.
cues.zh: 當然不是全部，統計更豐富，但幾乎一切，都能以某種方式連回這個簡單算式。

cues.en: And this simple expression is also related to some really bizarre features about, features about mathematics and the universe
cues.zh: 它也關聯到數學與宇宙中，一些非常奇妙的特性，

cues.en: that we often take for granted when you're in a course.
cues.zh: 上課時常被我們視為理所當然。

cues.en: But things like the law of large numbers, which is a weird thing, and the central limit theorem, these are all fancy sounding terms, but they reveal some fundamental features
cues.zh: 例如大數法則，這是奇妙的事，還有中央極限定理，聽起來華麗，卻揭示，

cues.en: of how our universe is put together.
cues.zh: 宇宙構成的某些根本特性。

cues.en: So the central limit theorem, for example, is important for statistical inference.
cues.zh: 例如，中央極限定理對統計推論很重要。

cues.en: You'll learn about it more later on in the course.
cues.zh: 稍後課程會深入學。

cues.en: But it essentially says that any sample distributions converged to a Gaussian, even if those distributions are not drawn from a Gaussian distribution.
cues.zh: 基本上說，任何樣本分布都會收斂成高斯，即使不是從高斯分布抽出。

cues.en: Now, basically that means that anytime you start going around and picking up random things, literally just picking up anything from anywhere in the entire universe,
cues.zh: 意思是，只要隨機到處收集東西，真的是宇宙任何地方的任何東西，

cues.en: and you put all of those things, all those collections of things into a pile, that pile is going to start looking like a Gaussian, even if those things have nothing to do with each other.
cues.zh: 把那些東西、那些集合堆在一起，就會開始像高斯，即使彼此毫無關係。

cues.en: This is also related to a phenomenon called regression to the mean, which you might've heard about.
cues.zh: 這也和「回歸平均值」現象有關，你可能聽過。

cues.en: It means that when things stray far off from the, you know, they start to get extreme on one end or the other, the next value is likely to be closer to the center of the distribution.
cues.zh: 意思是，當事情偏離很遠，變得非常極端，下一個值很可能更接近分布中心。

cues.en: And there's something that's almost philosophical about this concept that we have this core component of us, what it means to be you, it's yourself,
cues.zh: 這個概念有點哲學意味：我們有核心部分，也就是你之所以為你的自我，

cues.en: and that some central concentration of your thoughts, your feelings, your behavioral characteristics, your patterns of interacting with the world.
cues.zh: 你的想法、感受、行為特徵，以及與世界互動的模式，會集中在某個中心。

cues.en: And regardless of whether you go below that or above that, you know, extreme sadness or extreme happiness, you're always going to return to your,
cues.zh: 不論低於或高於它，極端悲傷或極端快樂，你總會回到，

cues.en: you know, this sort of essence of who you are.
cues.zh: 自己是誰的某種本質。

cues.en: And that is somewhere close to the peak of this distribution.
cues.zh: 那個位置就在分布峰附近。

cues.en: So there's just something very beautiful and I think very meaningful and deep about the simplicity of the normal equation, the Gaussian distribution.
cues.zh: 常態公式、高斯分布的簡單，讓我覺得非常美，也很有意義、很深刻。

cues.en: Okay, so that's the end of this little tangent.
cues.zh: 這個小離題到此結束。

cues.en: We're gonna get back to the practical aspects of learning about statistics.
cues.zh: 回到學統計的實際面。

cues.en: But I do want to encourage you every now and then, you don't have to do this all the time.
cues.zh: 不過，鼓勵你偶爾這麼做，不必一直如此。

cues.en: But every once in a while, just take a moment to try to appreciate the beauty of mathematics and the weird simplicity of mathematics.
cues.zh: 但偶爾花一點時間，欣賞數學的美與奇妙的簡單。

cues.en: In addition to trying to understand why we are learning this stuff and how it is relevant for practical aspects of day-to-day life.
cues.zh: 除了理解為何學這些，以及如何應用於日常實務，也欣賞它。
